fields.mechanism: Hydrogel swelling creates a self-regulating seal that provides a non-zero cracking pressure and prevents reverse flow leakage without relying on moving mechanical parts or filters.
fields.intervention: Integrate a hydrogel-based sealing element into the shunt valve design that swells in response to fluid exposure to maintain valve patency and prevent backflow, eliminating components prone to mechanical blockage.
fields.expected_effect: The valve remains patent and prevents blockage of the shunt pathway while maintaining effective intracranial pressure control.
fields.falsification_test: Subject the modified valve to chronic exposure to ex vivo cerebrospinal fluid and test for clogging or occlusion of the flow path over an extended period; failure is defined by a significant increase in flow resistance or complete blockage.

fields.mechanism: Hydrogel swelling provides a self-contained fluidic barrier that creates a non-zero cracking pressure for forward flow while physically eliminating the reverse-flow path.
fields.intervention: Replace the static mechanical shunt valve orifice with a swellable hydrogel membrane designed to expand and seal the reverse-flow pathway in the event of negative pressure.
fields.expected_effect: The shunt valve maintains patency for forward CSF drainage while becoming fully occluded to reverse flow, thereby preventing the backflow of peritoneal bacteria or debris that typically cause chronic blockage and infection.
fields.falsification_test: Subject the hydrogel valve to a standardized reverse pressure cycle in a physiological saline environment; if measurable reverse flow exceeds the threshold during the test, the mechanism fails to prevent the specific blockage pathway.

Replace standard mechanical occlusion components in the shunt valve with a hydrogel-based check-valve element that swells to seal against backflow and requires specific pressure to open
The valve remains patent and prevents blockage of the shunt pathway while maintaining effective intracranial pressure control.

The shunt valve maintains patency for forward CSF drainage while becoming fully occluded to reverse flow, thereby preventing the backflow of peritoneal bacteria or debris that typically cause chronic blockage and infection.
